cards.title: Exact directed maximum flow in \(O((m+n) \operatorname{polylog} n)\) time
cards.formal:
For every fixed integer \(a\ge1\), do there exist a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm \(A_a\), integers \(B_a\ge a+3\), \(k_a\ge0\) and \(C_a\ge1\) with the following property? On every explicitly represented directed graph \(G\) with \(n\ge2\) vertices, \(m\) arcs, distinct terminals \(s,t\), and integer arc capacities
\[0\le u_e\le n^a,\]
the algorithm uses words of \(w=B_a\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) bits, halts on every random execution within
\[C_a(m+n)\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil^{k_a}\]
word operations, and outputs an exact integral maximum \(s\)-\(t\) flow with probability at least \(2/3\)?
The output must give a flow value on every original arc. The algorithm, constants and logarithmic exponent may depend on \(a\), but not on the graph, its capacities, its terminal choices or its input ordering. The complete graph, flow and machine conventions are specified below.
cards.definitions:
Graph and representation. The vertex set is \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). An ordered arc list \((e_1,\ldots,e_m)\) consists of distinct ordered pairs \(e_j=(x_j,y_j)\in[n]^2\) with \(x_j\ne y_j\), so \(0\le m\le n(n-1)\). Opposite arcs may both occur and have independent capacities; parallel copies of the same ordered pair and loops are excluded. The graph may be disconnected and may contain isolated vertices and zero-capacity arcs. The terminals \(s,t\in[n]\) are distinct. The input is an array of machine words containing the header \((n,m,s,t)\), the list \(1,\ldots,n\) of vertices, and the triples \((x_j,y_j,u_{e_j})\) in the given arc order. Correctness and time bounds hold for every ordering. Capacities and labels are unsigned integers, each in one word. The explicit vertex list fixes the \(m+n\) convention even when \(m=0\). There is no succinct representation, adjacency oracle or precomputed index.

Feasible flow and optimum. A flow is a list \(f=(f_{e_1},\ldots,f_{e_m})\) of integers with \(0\le f_e\le u_e\) on every arc and
\[\sum_{e=(x,v)}f_e=\sum_{e=(v,y)}f_e\qquad\text{for every }v\in[n]\setminus\{s,t\}.\]
Each sum ranges over the arcs actually present. Its value is the net flow leaving the source,
\[\operatorname{val}(f)=\sum_{e=(s,y)}f_e-\sum_{e=(x,s)}f_e.\]
Incoming arcs at \(s\), outgoing arcs at \(t\), and circulations are allowed. Conservation implies that this equals the net flow entering \(t\). Define \(F(G,u,s,t)\) as the largest value among the feasible integral flows. The set of such flows is finite and nonempty because the all-zero list is feasible, so the maximum is attained and nonnegative. Also \(F\le(n-1)n^a\). The usual integral-flow theorem identifies this optimum with the real-valued maximum flow for integral capacities. A successful output is the list of exactly \(m\) integers in original arc order that forms a feasible flow with value \(F\). No prescribed tie-breaking between different optimal flows is required. If \(m=0\), the empty list is the correct output.

Machine model. Put \(L_n=\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\), so each word contains \(w=B_aL_n\) bits. A word stores an integer in \(\{0,\ldots,2^w-1\}\). The random-access machine has a fixed finite program, a fixed finite set of registers and word-addressed memory; input words occupy the initial array and other memory is initially zero. Each executed instruction costs one operation. Allowed instructions are word reads and writes, moves, conditional branches, comparisons, bitwise Boolean operations, logical shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), and unsigned integer division with a nonzero divisor. A logical shift by at least \(w\) returns zero. A memory address must fit in one word. Input, output and all memory used must fit within the address space, with \(B_a\) chosen as part of the algorithm's fixed constants. Arithmetic on more than one word must be implemented using these operations and charged accordingly. Exact real arithmetic is not a unit-cost instruction.

Randomness and resources. A random-word instruction returns a fresh independent uniform element of \(\{0,\ldots,2^w-1\}\) at cost one; equivalently its bits are independent fair bits. The success probability is over this sequence for each fixed valid input. A run outside the successful event may return a failure marker or an incorrect result, but must obey the same time bound. All graph preprocessing, memory accesses, random generation and writing of output words are charged. The bound is on the total running time of every run of this one static computation, not merely on expected time or on typical executions. An amortized analysis of internal operations is permitted if it establishes this total bound. There are no oracles, quantum operations, input-dependent advice or free preprocessing. Behavior outside the stated input promises is unrestricted.

Uniformity and quantifiers. For each fixed \(a\), one finite program works for all \(n,m,G,u,s,t\); it cannot contain a table or different advice indexed by \(n\). The quantifier order is
\[\forall a\ge1\ \exists A_a,B_a,k_a,C_a\ \forall(G,u,s,t).\]
The selected target does not additionally require an effective procedure that constructs \(A_a\) from \(a\), a common logarithmic exponent for all \(a\), or a bound polynomial in \(a\). For each fixed \(a\), however, \(k_a\) is a single integer independent of input size. The explicit running-time expression is precisely the meaning of the title's \(O((m+n)\operatorname{polylog}n)\).
cards.answer_criterion: Provide a complete, mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the existence proposition or its logical negation. An affirmative proof must establish, for each fixed capacity exponent \(a\), one program and fixed constants satisfying both the every-run time bound and the per-input success probability, including exact integral feasibility and optimality of all output arc values. A deterministic algorithm with that bound also qualifies. A negative proof must establish a fixed \(a\ge1\) for which every uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm in this model having any such fixed-polylogarithmic worst-case bound has some valid instance with success probability strictly below \(2/3\). A lower bound for one flow framework, an oracle-only algorithm, or a conditional conjecture does not prove that universal negation. A \((1-\varepsilon)\)-approximate flow, the optimum value alone, an algorithm for a restricted graph class, or a bound of \((m+n)^{1+o(1)}\) without the required fixed logarithmic overhead is insufficient. The algorithmic exact-flow requirement is retained; numerical benchmark tolerance does not replace its output specification.
cards.why: Maximum flow is a central primitive for routing, cuts and combinatorial optimization. Almost-linear algorithms have already removed a polynomial overhead. This question asks whether exact directed flow can be computed with only a fixed power of a logarithm beyond explicit input size, on all polynomial-capacity instances and with a complete flow as output.

importance.reason: A central static graph optimization primitive with broad algorithmic consequences. The precise remaining overhead separates the established almost-linear breakthrough from the longstanding nearly linear target; this is a general problem rather than a refinement of one fixed algorithm.

progress.text: The first almost-linear exact maximum-flow and minimum-cost-flow preprint is submitted; the checked April revision states the precise capacity dependence.
A deterministic almost-linear exact-flow algorithm is posted, removing randomization while retaining subpolynomial overhead.
The duality framework improves the explicit subpolynomial overheads for static exact flow, alongside its decremental results.
ICALP2026 publishes a faster undirected approximate-flow algorithm with fixed logarithmic factors and inverse-error dependence.
Li and Wice give a different almost-linear maximum-flow framework without the outer interior-point loop. Their stated final bound is still almost-linear.

context_blocks.text: Capacity constraints bound how much can travel along each arc, while conservation couples choices throughout the network. Exactness asks for the largest transferable amount, not merely a feasible routing. Because capacities are integral, an integral optimum exists, but the algorithm still has to find an optimal routing among many interacting possibilities.

The logarithmic overhead is the unresolved guarantee. For example, \(h(n)=2^{\sqrt{\log_2(n+2)}}\) satisfies \(h(n)=n^{o(1)}\), yet exceeds \((\log_2(n+2))^k\) for every fixed \(k\) once \(n\) is sufficiently large. Thus almost-linear and fixed-polylogarithmic time bounds are different. In this simple directed-graph format, \(n\le m+n\le n^2\), so logarithms of input word count and vertex count differ by only a constant factor.

Chen and coauthors’ 2022 breakthrough computes exact maximum flow in \(m^{1+o(1)}\log U\) time with high probability for integral capacities bounded by \(U\). For \(U\le n^a\), the capacity term is logarithmic, while the subpolynomial graph-size overhead remains. Their analysis uses fixed-point quantities with polynomially many logarithmic bits; charging multiword arithmetic does not turn that overhead into a fixed logarithmic power.

The 2023 deterministic algorithm of van den Brand and coauthors also obtains exact almost-linear flow. The 2024 duality paper further improves the stated static bounds: its Theorem 6.17 gives randomized \(m\,2^{O((\log m)^{3/4}\log\log m)}\) time and deterministic \(m\,2^{O((\log m)^{5/6}\log\log m)}\) time for polynomially bounded integral minimum-cost flow. These are still guarantees with subpolynomial overhead, rather than the fixed logarithmic bound requested here.

Li and Wice’s August 2026 manuscript removes the outer interior-point loop from another almost-linear maximum-flow framework. Its deterministic pseudo-circulation subroutine is combined with a randomized balanced-graph flow routine, and the stated final result remains almost-linear. The deterministic nature of an intermediate step does not make the full reduction deterministic, and removing the outer loop does not itself establish fixed-polylogarithmic overhead.

The ICALP 2026 algorithm of Fleischmann, George Z. Li and Jason Li has fixed-polylogarithmic overhead for constant-accuracy approximate flow on undirected graphs. Both qualifications matter: the present task concerns arbitrary directed graphs and exact integral output, and that approximation theorem has additional inverse-error dependence. It does not directly establish the target here.

An approximation with a fixed relative error need not determine an integer optimum whose magnitude grows with the input. Likewise, finding only an optimal value does not fulfill the requested output list. Polynomially bounded capacities ensure each input capacity and output arc value fits in a logarithmic number of bits; the question does not hide arbitrarily long integers behind unit-cost input access.

source_formulation.text: The retained target is the user-selected fixed-polylogarithmic overhead for exact directed maximum flow with capacities at most n^a, for every fixed a. The cited exact-flow papers provide almost-linear benchmarks, not statements that their subpolynomial overhead is already a fixed logarithmic power. The m+n convention, per-a word length and worst-case randomized time are explicit editorial model choices preserved from admission.

sentences: An exact maximum flow routes the largest possible integral amount between two terminals while obeying every arc capacity and intermediate conservation law.
For each fixed polynomial bound on capacities, the question asks for one algorithm whose time is input size times a single fixed power of a logarithm.
The specified randomized word-RAM must respect that total time on every execution and return a complete optimal flow with probability at least two thirds on each valid input.
A complete Lean proof must supply the algorithm and both guarantees or rule out all such algorithms for some fixed capacity exponent.
The checked exact almost-linear algorithms and undirected approximation results do not establish this fixed-polylogarithmic exact directed-flow target.

checked_sources: Read official arXiv:2203.00671 revision history (1 March2022v1,22 April2022v2), cached full abstract, introduction, Theorem1.1 and Corollary1.2, and §3 fixed-point computational model. The exact maximum-flow guarantee is m^{1+o(1)} logU with high probability; fixed-point word lengths are polylogarithmic in input encoding. JACM72(3),2025 metadata is corroborated by the August2026 paper’s bibliography; a separate journal proof was not inspected.

Read official arXiv:2309.16629 record, cached full abstract, §1.2 Theorem1.1 and §2 model. The algorithm is deterministic and almost-linear, with integral input and logarithmic capacity/cost dependence. Checked the authors’ institutional publication listings for FOCS2023. Did not conflate this2023 paper with the separate FOCS2024 duality paper.

Read arXiv:2407.10830 primary abstract, cached introduction’s static application and §6.2 Theorem6.17 with its stated exact rounding conclusion. Explicit overheads are2^{O((logm)^{3/4}loglogm)} randomized and2^{O((logm)^{5/6}loglogm)} deterministic; neither displayed guarantee is fixed-polylogarithmic. Full data-structure and rounding proofs were not independently audited.

Read official arXiv:2608.17384v1 record (18 August2026), cached full abstract and §§1–2: deterministic pseudo-circulation Theorem3, balanced-flow Theorem6 with randomized running time, and final rounding plus residual iterations. The manuscript title page says19 August but the submission date is18 August. The stated final max-flow bound remains m^{1+o(1)}; no inference of full deterministic complexity was made from Theorem3 alone.

Read official Dagstuhl ICALP2026 article91 full abstract, introduction and Theorem1 via the publisher HTML, cached as flow-weak2026.txt. The theorem treats undirected graphs and a (1-epsilon)-approximation, with runtime O(m log^9 n loglogn+epsilon^{-1}m log^6 n). It does not solve exact directed flow in the selected bound; full proof not independently audited.

Bounded primary-source searches through16 September2026 found no matching fixed-polylogarithmic-overhead exact directed-flow result. Screened official abstracts of arXiv:2604.04752 (DAG projections and parallel reductions) and ICALP2026 flow-space/approximation results at their different guarantees; no matching resolution was inferred. Search results unrelated to network-flow algorithms were excluded. No exhaustive search or independent source-proof certification is claimed, and archived card bodies were not opened.

Checked that explicit simple graphs satisfy n<=m+n<=n^2, capacity and total-flow bit lengths are O_a(logn), isolated vertices justify the m+n convention, and a fixed logarithmic exponent is stronger than a generic subpolynomial overhead. The output remains the complete exact integral flow, consistent with the inherited yes/no algorithm-existence target.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards, including resolved records, are archived outside the ranking without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
